name: J/L Cut Dialogue Smoothing
use_when: A talking-head, interview, tutorial, voiceover, or screen-recording cut feels harsh.
The editor needs to remove pauses while keeping speech natural.
A short-form talking-head cut needs tight overlap around silence and speech starts.
Silences and bad takes have been removed but the remaining dialogue cuts still feel rough.
A visual cut can be hidden by letting audio lead or trail the picture.
avoid_when: The audio lead would misrepresent who is speaking or what happened.
The cut needs to feel abrupt for comedy, shock, or emphasis.
Room tone or background noise changes so much that the split becomes obvious.

timeline_pattern.j_cut_rule: Let the next audio begin before the next image when it improves flow or hides a visual jump.
timeline_pattern.l_cut_rule: Let previous audio continue under the next image when the viewer needs continuity or context.
timeline_pattern.crossfade_rule: Use short audio crossfades or room tone when hard audio edges are distracting.
timeline_pattern.premiere_alt_video_rule: In Premiere, Alt-select or otherwise separate the video layer so picture can overlap audio without moving the spoken timing.

motion.rule: Use a punch-in, B-roll, slide, or overlay to hide the visual discontinuity only when it supports the spoken point.

sound.rule: Keep the speech rhythm natural and remove only pauses that do not carry meaning.

keyframe_values.audio_crossfade: Start with 2-6 frames for tight speech cuts; extend only if room tone needs smoothing.
keyframe_values.short_form_dead_air: Remove dead air over 300 ms unless it creates tension, humor, or emotional value.

captions.rule: Caption timing follows the audible speech, not the visual cut point.

color.rule: No direct color rule; avoid grade jumps when the visual cut is already being smoothed.

implementation.ffmpeg: Split audio and video streams in the edit decision data, use atrim/acrossfade for audio overlaps, and concat the final picture timing after review.
implementation.remotion: Allow audio components to start before or continue after the visible clip Sequence; store overlapFrames and captionStartFrame separately.
implementation.blender: Use only for animated explainers when narration should lead a visual transition.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Extract audio or unlink clip audio, trim video separately, then add short audio fades between spoken clips.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Unlink, expand tracks, or Alt-select video independently, overlap picture and sound around the cut, use rolling edits on audio edges, and add constant-power audio transitions when needed.

common_mistakes: Cutting video and audio at the same hard frame when the speech needs a smoother bridge.
Removing meaningful breath or thinking time that created human rhythm.
Letting the audio go visibly out of sync with mouth movement.
Using a J/L cut to hide a misleading rearrangement.
Overlapping short-form cuts so tightly that speech feels chopped or unnatural.
Removing silences but leaving every picture and audio edit on the same hard frame.
qc: Does speech sound natural when watched without looking at the timeline?
Does the visual cut avoid a distracting face or eye jump?
Do captions match the audible line timing?
Is any removed silence truly dead air rather than emotional pacing?
Do overlapped short-form cuts preserve natural speech rhythm?
After silence removal, do dialogue cuts flow naturally without visible or audible jolts?
